key_sentences: Water-based alkaline cleaner for removing oil and grease from metal surfaces in industrial settings.
The mixture does not contain substances assessed as PBT or vPvB.
Contact with the eyes causes pain, redness and a risk of permanent damage.
Absorb spills with sand or another inert material and place in a closed container for disposal.
Store in the original container at temperatures between 5 °C and 35 °C.
Contact with strong acids releases heat.
This safety data sheet replaces all earlier versions.

rows: Merrow Chemical Products Ltd. Unit 12, Riverside Works, Leek ST13 6DT, United Kingdom
Acute Tox. 4, H302, H312, H332 Skin Irrit. 2, H315; Eye Irrit. 2, H319
Met. Corr. 1, H290 Skin Corr. 1B, H314; STOT SE 3, H335
Acute Tox. 4, H302 Eye Dam. 1, H318
Nitrile rubber gloves, thickness at least 0.4 mm, breakthrough time over 480 minutes (EN ISO 374).
Not normally required; use a filter mask type A2/P2 when spraying in confined spaces.

list_items.text: P280 Wear protective gloves and eye protection.
P301+P312 IF SWALLOWED: Call a POISON CENTRE or doctor if you feel unwell.
P305+P351+P338 IF IN EYES: Rinse cautiously with water for several minutes. Remove contact lenses, if present and easy to do. Continue rinsing.
P501 Dispose of contents and container in accordance with local regulations.
After inhalation: move the person to fresh air and keep at rest.
After skin contact: remove contaminated clothing and wash the skin with plenty of water.
After eye contact: rinse immediately with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes.
Hold the eyelids apart while rinsing.
After ingestion: rinse the mouth with water. Do not induce vomiting.

notes: Safety data sheet in Arial Narrow, three pages. Furniture: the running header (document type and product on the left, revision and date on the right; listed once), the footer company name (listed once) and 'Page 1 of 3' … 'Page 3 of 3'. The regulation line under the title is a subtitle in body text. Section bars 'SECTION n: …' are level-2 headings; numbered subsections '1.1 …' are level-3 headings (underlined). Sections 11–15 are deliberately absent from this abridged sheet; numbering jumps from 10 to 16. Key/value blocks (product identifier, supplier, exposure controls) are borderless tables without a header row; the supplier cell has two lines joined with one space; the key '1.4 Emergency telephone number' sits inside that table and is not a heading. Grids: the hazard table, the composition table (cells of two lines joined with one space; concentration cells read e.g. '5 – < 10'), the exposure-limit table with a two-level header ('Substance' and 'Source' span two rows; each limit spans 'ppm' and 'mg/m³'; both header rows given) and the properties table. The signal word DANGER is in a red letter-spaced frame (body text). Precautionary statements are a TYPED list whose markers are the P-codes (e.g. 'P280', 'P301+P312') set in a hanging column; first-aid measures are a CSS-drawn square-bullet list with a nested square-bullet list (markers not in the text).
